root_idea.summary: The root preserves two principal lexical poles: camel terminology and animal dung.
root_idea.development: Its lexical branches extend from the designation of a camel and the dung it produces to verbs for voiding, throwing, cleaning, or causing dung to soil a milker, as well as terms for dung-containing bodily passages and animals characterized by such behavior.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun بَعِير is displayed under its normalized Classical Arabic citation form.

senses.definition: A camel, whether male or female.
senses.usage_conditions: A general designation that applies to either sex. In the supplied Quranic occurrences it appears in the construction حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ, a camel-associated load.

senses.definition: A beast of burden or carrier, including an ass.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quran 12:72, the word is attested with the sense of an ass or, more broadly, anything that carries; in حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ it identifies the carrier associated with the measured load.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of animals, especially camels, sheep, and goats, and of certain other specified hooved animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw a piece of animal dung at someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use in which a piece of بَعْر is used as the object thrown.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a widow to throw away the final piece of dung marking the completion of her waiting period before remarriage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression referring to the traditional act that ended the widow's prescribed waiting period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a camel to become a بَعِير.
To foul one's milker with dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a ewe, she-goat, or she-camel; the act is regarded as a fault because dung may fall into the milking vessel.
Said of a ewe, goat, or camel in the cited construction بَاعَرَتْ إِلَى حَالِبِهَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clean an intestine or gut of its dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use referring to removing dung from the intestine or gut.
A collective noun for dung of camels, sheep, goats, and similar animals, as well as certain other specified hooved animals; its individual noun and plural forms are also attested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fouling of a milker with dung by a ewe, she-goat, or she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The act is treated as a fault because the dung may be cast into the milking vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A widow who throws the final piece of dung to mark the end of her waiting period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized designation connected with the traditional widow's waiting-period idiom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place or passage of dung, especially the rectum or intestine containing it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of the dung-containing passage of a quadruped; the plural is مَبَاعِرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal that fouls its milker with dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a ewe, she-goat, or she-camel characterized by this behavior.
